(a) the ELBO is an upper bound on the log-likelihood of a model with a continuous latent variable and (b) this bound can be optimized by stochastic gradient descent.

(i) we introduce a stochastic variation inference and learning algorithm for intractable models that scales to large data, (ii) we show that for intractable i.i.d. models, posterior inference can become very efficient by fitting an inference model to the intractible posterior, (iii) we provide a theoretical analysis of our algorithm that shows that it converges to a local optimum of the true variational bound.

(1) the ELBO can be reparameterized in such a way that it is a differentiable function of the variational distribution and (2) this reparameterization can be used for stochastic variational inference in the intractability case, as well as in the tractability case, where posterior inference is made especially efficient by learning an inference model.

we propose an auto-encoding variational bayes (AEVB) framework, where the variational posterior q is implemented with a neural network, which we call the recognition network, and the evidence lower bound is optimized by stochastic gradient ascent in a variational auto-encoder (VAE) fashion.
Auto-Encoder Variational Bayes can be used for both approximate inference and learning in intractable probabilistic models.
